title: Review of Enforcement Agencies' Investigation Protocols for Teenagers and Those with Special Needs
what_it_is: Review of Enforcement Agencies' Investigation Protocols for Teenagers and Those with Special Needs

sections.label: Questions on minors and criminal justice
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Home Affairs about arrested minors' mental health, deaths, investigations, support, and identification of vulnerable persons.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs regarding persons under 18 years old who were arrested by the Police in the past five years (a) what proportion had a history of mental health conditions; (b) how many were hospitalised or died subsequently whilst under Police investigation; (c) what were the reasons for these hospitalisation cases and deaths; (d) what were the outcomes of the investigations following the arrests; and (e) what support is available to young persons with mental health conditions facing Police investigation or arrest.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) how do law enforcement agencies identify vulnerable persons and persons with mental disorders or disabilities when they interact with the criminal justice system at first contact; (b) who conducts these assessments in the law enforcement agencies; and (c) whether law enforcement agencies are adequately staffed with qualified professionals to make these assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in drug-related investigations involving minors, what are the approach and safeguards taken by the Central Narcotics Bureau especially in cases where the minor has a history of medical or mental health issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) how can family members of a young person, whose death is suspected to be related to the person’s interaction with the criminal justice system, can request for a formal investigation into the death; (b) what are the criteria used to evaluate the need for such investigations; (c) how does the Government ensure that investigations are undertaken with neutrality by an independent party; and (d) whether the Government is committed to provide to the family the outcomes from the investigation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: A summary of CNB’s investigations was released on 22 October 2021.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: They show, in essence: Justin Lee had been advertising the sale of LSD stamps, a Class A controlled drug, on a messaging app.

sections.label: No Appropriate Adult for Justin
sections.summary: Since Justin was 17 years old, there was no Appropriate Adult.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Since Justin was 17 years old, there was no Appropriate Adult.

sections.label: Justin mentioned depression diagnosis
sections.summary: During the first video-recorded interview, Justin told the Investigation Officer he had previously been diagnosed with depression.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: During the first video-recorded interview, Justin mentioned to the Investigation Officer (IO) that he had previously been diagnosed with depression.

sections.label: Toxicology found LSD and Nitrazepam
sections.summary: A Health Sciences Authority toxicology report showed traces of LSD and Nitrazepam in Justin's urine and blood when he fell to his death.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Toxicology report from the Health Sciences Authority showed traces of LSD and Nitrazepam in Justin’s urine and blood when he fell to his death.

sections.label: AAYS scheme extension decision
sections.summary: The current process announced in 2017 was operationalised for a period while considering issues, with a decision in the next few months on extending the AAYS scheme to 16- and 17-year-olds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, we decided to operationalise the current process, which was announced in 2017, for a period first, while we consider if, and, if so, how we can deal with the issues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will announce our decision in the next few months as to whether we can extend the AAYS scheme to persons who are 16 and 17 years old.

sections.label: Prosecution outcomes for arrested minors
sections.summary: Of 9,485 persons under 18 arrested from 2016 to 2020, only 16% were prosecuted, so 84% were not prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Regarding the outcomes of the investigations, out of 9,485 persons under 18 years old arrested from 2016 to 2020, only 16% were prosecuted; so, 84% were not prosecuted.

sections.label: Coroners Act reportable deaths
sections.summary: Under the Coroners Act, both scenarios are reportable deaths and the Police must investigate the cause.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Under the Coroners Act, both scenarios would be deemed as reportable deaths, and the Police must investigate the cause of the death.

sections.label: Justin not in custody
sections.summary: Justin was not in custody when he passed away in September.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Specific to Justin, we need to be clear: Justin was not in custody at the time of his passing away in September.

sections.label: Appropriate Adult question answered
sections.summary: The question on whether an Appropriate Adult was present during Justin's interviews was already answered at the start of the reply.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Regarding Mr Leong Mun Wai’s question on whether an Appropriate Adult was present during Justin’s interviews, I have already answered it at the beginning of my reply.

sections.label: CNB officer training protocols
sections.summary: New CNB officers learn protocols for young suspects and persons with mental disabilities, and all officers undergo refresher training and an annual proficiency test.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As part of the core skills training for new CNB officers, they learn the protocols to handle young suspects and persons with mental disabilities, such as the Appropriate Adult schemes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And all officers, in fact, undergo refresher training on how to manage such suspects and offenders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: They are also required to pass an annual proficiency test to ensure that they are proficient in handling young suspects and persons with mental disabilities.

sections.label: Cut-off age for protections
sections.summary: The question asks whether MHA does not accept that the spirit requires all measures protecting young suspects to have a cut-off age of 18 instead of 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does MHA then not accept the fact that the spirit of that would require all measures protecting young suspects to have a cut-off age of 18 instead of 16?

sections.label: Family members assisting investigations
sections.summary: The question asks whether law enforcement agencies allow family members to assist investigations for non-verbal or non-communicative special needs suspects, and the review outcome will be announced in the next few months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Some of the special needs suspects may actually be non-verbal or non-communicative and perhaps only the family members understand what he or she is trying to say.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask whether law enforcement agencies do allow family members to assist in the investigation process so that the communication can be better understood?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, indeed, as I have shared earlier, we are reviewing it and as such, we will announce the outcome of the review in the next few months.

sections.label: Volunteer numbers for youth schemes
sections.summary: There are about 331 AAYS volunteers and 320 AAPMD volunteers, and expanding AAYS to ages 16 and 17 would require doubling the volunteer pool.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Currently, we have about 331 volunteers for the AAYS and 320 volunteers for the AAPMD.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As an estimate, if we expand the AAYS to cover suspects aged 16 and 17, we will need to increase the pool of volunteers to double of what we have today.

sections.label: Activating something during investigations
sections.summary: Even if the person does not ask for it, it will be activated when it is felt to help the investigation process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Even if the person does not ask for it, when we feel that it helps in the investigation process, we will activate it.
